answer: Glacier-ripened staking makes time the sybil barrier. Each identity locks coins in a glacier contract for a long freeze, unmoveable and unshareable across keys. Weight is a nectar score ripening with freeze time: below the zenith it counts for little, and full mining power unlocks only at the zenith; the score is identity-bound, non-transferable, and slashed on early exit. An attacker with N sybils must freeze N stakes for the full window, as one sum cannot be recycled across identities. Majority weight then demands N-fold capital dormant for months, far costlier than throwaway accounts.
